analytical_question: Can this organization absorb, govern and sustain a voluntary station-level evaluation now, and what readiness gaps block it?
general_et_finding: Passive back-support exoskeletons offer task-dependent assistance, but potential load or comfort benefits do not establish long-term injury prevention. The selected sources do not establish device-specific effectiveness for this site; fit and new hazards require evaluation [E1-E2].
application_finding: Conditional application fit: the bounded palletizing task is a candidate for qualified evaluation after feasible task redesign. No local fit, comfort or movement outcome is available. Existing handling aids, load limits and task exclusions must remain in place; an exoskeleton is not justification for heavier or faster work [E1,E3].
organization_specific_finding: NOT_READY. Leadership and sponsorship: GAP - Director supports exploration, but no signed charter or stop authority is assigned. Skills and training: GAP - No ergonomist or trained fitting staff; qualified assessment capacity is absent. Workflow and process: GAP - Lift table and rotation are strengths; residual risk assessment and SOP are absent. Infrastructure and data: GAP - Baseline, storage, cleaning and inspection arrangements are absent; size compatibility is unknown. Resources and budget: GAP - $4,000 buying allowance is a strength, but paid training, backfill and recurring support are unfunded. Governance and risk: GAP - No trial risk review or withdrawal/incident procedure exists. Culture and change: GAP - No worker consultation; throughput pressure threatens voluntary use. Operating ownership: GAP - Purchasing can buy devices; daily fitting, cleaning, inspection and withdrawal have no owner. Readiness classification is an inference from this fictional case, not a technology maturity rating.

evidence.claim: Task-specific potential benefit; fit, mobility and transferred risks require evaluation; address residual risk after feasible engineering controls.
evidence.evidence_type: Original agency guidance or research synthesis
evidence.notes: Older research commentary, not a device certification or proof of long-term injury reduction. Do not treat its research snapshot as the entire 2026 evidence base.

evidence.claim: Workplace wearable adoption can face cost and usability barriers; published efficacy evidence is limited.
evidence.evidence_type: Original agency guidance or research synthesis
evidence.notes: Broad wearable overview. Sensor privacy issues cannot automatically be attributed to a passive device with no electronics.

evidence.claim: Design work and job demands around worker capabilities; evaluate physical and psychosocial risk factors.
evidence.evidence_type: Original agency guidance or research synthesis
evidence.notes: General methodological guidance, not a local task assessment or a legal opinion.

evidence.claim: Organizational arrangements used for this conditional assessment are supplied in the case.
evidence.evidence_type: Fictional test premise, not empirical organization evidence
evidence.notes: No site observation, interview, procurement quote or physical trial occurred.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Potential assistance does not prove a net safety benefit or long-term injury reduction.
No model-specific fit assessment or local outcome data exist. General sources are dated and are not an exhaustive 2026 review.
Site attributes, budgets and allocations are assumed for testing. Real deployment requires verified records and competent human approval.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in NOT_READY given explicit ownership and governance gaps; low confidence in actual device value. No medical or legal determination is made.
value_opportunity_implication: A bounded evaluation could establish whether workers find support useful and whether the operating burden is sustainable. No savings, productivity uplift or injury reduction is quantified.
risk_governance_implication: Keep qualified human assessment, worker withdrawal and independent stop authority. Do not substitute wearables for feasible task redesign. The selected devices have no electronics; cloud infrastructure, charging and tracking controls are not assumed needs.
recommendation_management_implication: P0 before any worker exposure: operations director (proposed accountable owner) must sign a charter assigning daily ownership and independent stop authority, fund qualified ergonomics support and protect voluntary participation; closure is a signed responsibility/authority record and funded staff allocation. P0: retained ergonomist and worker representatives (proposed roles) must document residual task risk, alternatives, fit/movement exclusions and an incident/withdrawal plan; safety lead signs trial review. P1 after P0: warehouse manager (proposed owner) budgets training/backfill and recurring care, creates fitting/cleaning/inspection SOPs and baselines, and obtains worker feedback without quota pressure; closure is approved budget, roster, competency records and SOP dry run. P2: review December 21, 2026; continue preparation only until all gates close, then reconsider a voluntary trial. Do not purchase devices merely to exhaust the allowance or authorize routine use now.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reassess at December 21, 2026 readiness review or sooner when authority, staffing, funding or worker-participation conditions change.
Pause any trial after reported pain, a new device-related hazard, unsafe movement or inability to withdraw; competent human review decides restart.
Reassess on device model, station, task, load or workforce-fit changes, or new credible effectiveness/safety evidence.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Who holds documented authority to stop use? Provide the signed station-specific risk review and incident/withdrawal procedure.
Provide model-specific compatibility information and local results before judging sustained benefit or scale readiness.
